# Embedding plot

## Single
```{r}
file_path <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "/4plot/IRIS_place_time_day_tsne.csv")
df_plot_word <- read.csv(file_path)

# Define your color scale limits
min_lat <- 48.6
max_lat <- 49.0

# Create the plot
p <- ggplot(df_plot_word, aes(x = x, y = y, color = center_lat)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    name = "Latitude",
    limits = c(min_lat, max_lat),
    #  low = "#4575b4", high = "#d73027", 
    low = "#263C7B", high = "#E9C62E",  
    oob = scales::squish               # Handle out-of-bound values
  ) +
  labs(title = "t-SNE of Location Embeddings color by lat") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major = element_line(size = 0.2),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
p
```

## All
only lat/lon
```{r}
# Define color scale limits
min_lat <- 48.6
max_lat <- 49.0
min_lon <- 2.0
max_lon <- 2.7

# List all CSV files in the directory
csv_files <- list.files(path = file.path(DATA_DIR, "4plot"), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)
# csv_files

# Define a function to create and save plots
plot_lat_lon <- function(df, base_name, method, variable, var_name, limits, suffix) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, color = !!sym(variable))) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c('#798234FF', '#A3AD62FF', '#D0D3A2FF', '#FDFBE4FF', '#F0C6C3FF', '#DF91A3FF', '#D46780FF'),
      name = var_name,
      limits = limits,
      oob = scales::squish
    ) +
    labs(title = paste(method, "colored by", var_name)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.major = element_line(size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  # Save the plot
  Fig_path <- file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig/word_by_latlon/")
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(Fig_path, paste0(base_name, "_", suffix, ".png")),
    plot = p,
    width = 9,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 600
  )
}

# Loop through each file
for (file_path in csv_files) {
  base_name <- str_remove(basename(file_path), "\\.csv")
  print(base_name)

  method <- str_extract(base_name, "[^_]+$") |> toupper()
  df <- read.csv(file_path)

  # Plot and save latitude
  plot_lat_lon(df, base_name, method, "center_lat", "Latitude", c(min_lat, max_lat), "lat")

  # Plot and save longitude
  plot_lat_lon(df, base_name, method, "center_lon", "Longitude", c(min_lon, max_lon), "lon")
}
```

by lat/lon/time/day
```{r}
# Define color scale limits
min_lat <- 48.6
max_lat <- 49.0
min_lon <- 2.0
max_lon <- 2.7

# Custom color mappings
time_colors <- c(
  "night" = "#798234",   # olive green
  "daytime" = "#D46780", # rose pink
  "evening" = "#F0C6C3FF"    # soft lime
)

day_type_colors <- c(
  "weekday" = "#DF91A3",   # muted pink
  "weekend" = "#798234"    # olive green
)

# List all CSV files in the directory
csv_files <- list.files(path = file.path(DATA_DIR, "4plot"), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)

# Create output directories if they don't exist
dir.create(file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig/word_by_latlon"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig/word_by_time"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig/word_by_day"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Function to plot latitude and longitude
plot_lat_lon <- function(df, base_name, method, variable, var_name, limits, suffix) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, color = !!sym(variable))) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c('#798234FF', '#A3AD62FF', '#D0D3A2FF', '#FDFBE4FF', '#F0C6C3FF', '#DF91A3FF', '#D46780FF'),
      name = var_name,
      limits = limits,
      oob = scales::squish
    ) +
    labs(title = paste(method, "colored by", var_name)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.major = element_line(size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  Fig_path <- file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig/word_by_latlon/")
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(Fig_path, paste0(base_name, "_", suffix, ".png")),
    plot = p,
    width = 9,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 600
  )
}

# Function to plot categorical variables with custom colors
plot_extra_var <- function(df, base_name, method, variable, var_name, folder_name) {
  # Select appropriate color mapping
  if (variable == "time") {
    custom_colors <- time_colors
  } else if (variable == "day_type") {
    custom_colors <- day_type_colors
  } else {
    stop("Unknown variable for custom color mapping.")
  }

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, color = !!sym(variable))) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = custom_colors, name = var_name) +
    labs(title = paste(method, "colored by", var_name)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.major = element_line(size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  Fig_path <- file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig", folder_name)
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(Fig_path, paste0(base_name, "_", variable, ".png")),
    plot = p,
    width = 9,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 600
  )
}

# Loop through each file
for (file_path in csv_files) {
  base_name <- str_remove(basename(file_path), "\\.csv")
  print(base_name)

  method <- str_extract(base_name, "[^_]+$") |> toupper()
  df <- read.csv(file_path)

  # Plot and save latitude
  plot_lat_lon(df, base_name, method, "center_lat", "Latitude", c(min_lat, max_lat), "lat")

  # Plot and save longitude
  plot_lat_lon(df, base_name, method, "center_lon", "Longitude", c(min_lon, max_lon), "lon")

  # Plot and save time if available
  if ("time" %in% names(df)) {
    plot_extra_var(df, base_name, method, "time", "Time", "word_by_time")
  }

  # Plot and save day_type if available
  if ("day_type" %in% names(df)) {
    plot_extra_var(df, base_name, method, "day_type", "Day Type", "word_by_day")
  }
}

```

### France
```{r}
# Set your desired color scale limits
sim_limits <- c(0.5, 0.8)  # adjust as needed

# Plot without x/y limits
p <- ggplot(place_sim_sf) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = sim_day_evening), color = "white", size = 0.01) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = armyrose_colors,
      name = "Similarity",
      limits = sim_limits,
      oob = squish
    ) +
    # theme_void() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Place-Level Temporal Similarity",
      subtitle = "Research Area: Day vs Night"
      # title = "Spatial Distribution of Day-Evening Similarity",
      # subtitle = "Colored by sim_day_evening values",
      # caption = "Source: place_sim_df"
    )

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig", "cosine_similarity/evening_all.png"),
  plot = p,
  width = 7,   # slightly wider
  height = 6.5,  # slightly taller
  dpi = 600
)
p
```

### Paris
```{r}
# Set x and y limits (longitude and latitude) for Paris
xlim_vals <- c(2.25, 2.45)  
ylim_vals <- c(48.78, 48.93)

# Plot
p <- ggplot(place_sim_sf) +
  # geom_sf(aes(fill = sim_day_evening), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  
  # Main place similarity polygons
  geom_sf(data = place_sim_sf, aes(fill = sim_day_evening), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  # Overlay boundary
  geom_sf(data = communes_sf, fill = NA, color = "black", stroke = 5) +
  
    scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = armyrose_colors,
    name = "Similarity",
    limits = sim_limits,
    oob = squish
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = xlim_vals, ylim = ylim_vals, expand = FALSE) +
  # theme_void() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
      # legend.position = "right",
    legend.position = c(1.15, 0.2),  # inside bottom-right corner
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),  # anchor bottom-right
    legend.key.height = unit(1.5, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Place-Level Temporal Similarity",
    subtitle = "Paris: Day vs Night"
    # subtitle = "Higher similarity = similar activity patterns between day and night; 
    # lower similarity = distinct temporal behavior",
    # caption = "Source: place_sim_df"
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig", "cosine_similarity/evening_Paris.png"),
  plot = p,
  width = 7,   # slightly wider
  height = 6.5,  # slightly taller
  dpi = 600
)
p
```

```{r}
# Load data
place_sim_df <- read.csv(file.path(DATA_DIR, "/4plot/word_place_similarity.csv"))
place_sim_sf <- st_as_sf(place_sim_df, wkt = "geometry", crs = 4326)

# Count NAs per column
na_counts <- colSums(is.na(place_sim_sf))
na_counts[na_counts > 0]
data.frame(
  column = names(na_counts),
  num_NA = na_counts
)

```

```{r}

# Columns to visualize
columns_to_plot <- c(
  "sim_day_evening",
  "sim_day_night",
  "sim_evening_night",
  "overall_sim",
  "temporal_distinctiveness"
)

# Titles & subtitles for each column
plot_titles <- c(
  sim_day_evening = "Place-Level Temporal Similarity",
  sim_day_night = "Place-Level Temporal Similarity",
  sim_evening_night = "Place-Level Temporal Similarity",
  overall_sim = "Overall Place Similarity",
  temporal_distinctiveness = "Temporal Distinctiveness"
)

plot_subtitles <- c(
  sim_day_evening = "Day vs Evening",
  sim_day_night = "Day vs Night",
  sim_evening_night = "Evening vs Night",
  overall_sim = "Overall Activity Similarity",
  temporal_distinctiveness = "How Different Temporal Patterns Are"
)

# File name suffixes
file_suffixes <- c(
  sim_day_evening = "day_evening",
  sim_day_night = "day_night",
  sim_evening_night = "evening_night",
  overall_sim = "overall",
  temporal_distinctiveness = "temporal"
)

# Color scale limits — adjust as needed per column if desired
sim_limits <- c(0.3, 0.8)  

# Paris map limits
xlim_vals <- c(2.25, 2.45)
ylim_vals <- c(48.78, 48.93)

# Loop over each column
for (col in columns_to_plot) {

  # Dynamically set plot aesthetics
  aes_fill <- aes_string(fill = col)

  # ============ GLOBAL MAP ============
  p_global <- ggplot(place_sim_sf) +
    geom_sf(aes_fill, color = "white", size = 0.01) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = armyrose_colors,
      name = "Similarity",
      limits = sim_limits,
      oob = squish
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = plot_titles[col],
      subtitle = plot_subtitles[col]
    )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig", "cosine_similarity", 
                         paste0("All_", file_suffixes[col], ".png")),
    plot = p_global,
    width = 7,
    height = 6.5,
    dpi = 600
  )

  # ============ PARIS ZOOMED MAP ============
  p_paris <- ggplot(place_sim_sf) +
    geom_sf(aes_fill, color = "white", size = 0.05) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = armyrose_colors,
      name = "Similarity",
      limits = sim_limits,
      oob = squish
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = xlim_vals, ylim = ylim_vals, expand = FALSE) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = c(1.15, 0.2),
      legend.justification = c(1, 0),
      legend.key.height = unit(1.5, "cm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = plot_titles[col],
      subtitle = paste0("Paris: ", plot_subtitles[col])
    )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(CODE_DIR, "fig", "cosine_similarity", 
                         paste0("Paris_", file_suffixes[col], ".png")),
    plot = p_paris,
    width = 7,
    height = 6.5,
    dpi = 600
  )
}
```
